description:
## Finding

JMAP-x2gd.64 ("`ChatBackend::update_object` `Ok(None)` vs
`Ok(Some(updated))` semantics are ambiguous when the backend
bumps `updatedAt` / membership counters on every successful
write") was filed as chat-server-local. The 3rd-pass confidence
note explicitly flagged this as "did NOT cross-check whether
mail-server's analogous method has the same ambiguity. If yes,
re-parent as workspace-canonical alongside .67's seven."

The cross-walk is now done. Result: **WORKSPACE-CANONICAL.**

## Evidence

**Chat-server** (`crate-jmap-chat-server/src/backend.rs:309-313`):

```
/// Apply a partial update (patch) to an existing object.
///
/// Returns `Some(updated_object)` if the backend modified any properties
/// beyond what the client requested (RFC 8620 §5.3 server-set field echo),
/// or `None` if the patch was applied verbatim.
```

**Mail-server** (`crate-jmap-mail-server/src/backend.rs:106-110`):

```
/// Apply a partial update (patch) to an existing object.
///
/// Returns `Some(updated_object)` if the backend modified any properties
/// beyond what the client requested (RFC 8620 §5.3 server-set field echo),
/// or `None` if the patch was applied verbatim.
```

The ambiguous sentence — "modified any properties beyond what the
client requested … or `None` if the patch was applied verbatim" —
is **byte-identical** in both crates. Both fail to address the
case where the backend timestamps every successful write
(`updatedAt`-equivalent fields exist on Mailbox / Email / Identity
on the mail side; on Space / Chat / Message on the chat side),
which makes the `None` branch unreachable on any production-grade
implementation.

Mail-server adds extra paragraphs (lines 112-119) covering
handler-side obligations and caller-context plumbing — useful but
orthogonal to the ambiguity. The core "modified beyond what the
client requested" phrase is the gap, and it is identical.

## Implication for fix planning

Per workspace AGENTS.md "Canonical Templates" rule:

> If you reshape this crate in a way that diverges from
> `jmap-mail-server`, change `jmap-mail-server` first, then
> propagate to every other extension-server sibling.

Fixing JMAP-x2gd.64 in chat-server alone is a regression of the
cookie-cutter intent. The fix MUST land in
`MailBackend::update_object` first, then propagate to all 8
extension-server siblings.

## Recommendation

Re-parent JMAP-x2gd.64 as workspace-canonical alongside the
seven findings in JMAP-x2gd.67 (.35 / .38 / .43 / .46 / .47 / .48 / .51).
Re-priced from "chat-server-local doc tightening" to
"workspace-canonical doc convention" — same priority, but the
fix surface expands to all extension-server crates.

## Engineering basis

Direct cross-walk of `crate-jmap-mail-server/src/backend.rs:106-119`
against `crate-jmap-chat-server/src/backend.rs:309-313`. The
identical-sentence finding is verifiable by `diff` of the two
doc-block ranges.

## What is NOT workspace-canonical

JMAP-x2gd.65 ("`apply_space_metadata_patch` `SetErrorType` selection
ambiguity") is **chat-server-LOCAL** — mail-server has no analog
method. All `MailBackend` partial-update paths route through the
generic `update_object`; mail-server has no semantic-mutation-key
split that would need a separate `apply_*_metadata_patch`. .65
stays as filed.

A broader workspace-canonical "name the `SetErrorType` variants on
every backend method that takes a wire blob ID or validates wire
values" finding is possible but would attach to
`create_object` / `update_object` / `import_email` / `copy_email`
generically, not to a metadata-patch method.
title: Workspace-canonical reclassification of JMAP-x2gd.64: update_object Ok(None)-vs-Some ambiguity is byte-identical in mail-server
